key_insight: A reduced-order fluid-structure model shows how peristalsis, porous drag, and compliant-wall motion jointly shape flow in a non-axisymmetric annular conduit like the periarterial space.
engineering_relevance: The model provides a mechanistic way to predict cerebrospinal fluid transport in porous, deformable channels and can guide design or interpretation of physiological flow studies.
method: Adds a Darcy–Brinkman drag term to represent porous resistance.
Couples the outer wall compliance to the fluid motion in a two-way FSI framework.
Reduces the coupled system to a single nonlinear PDE for axial pressure; small-amplitude cases admit analytical solutions.
evidence_signal: The paper presents a reduced-order analytical/perturbative model and uses it for parametric studies rather than reporting new experimental data in the abstract.
watch_item: The reduction and analytical results rely on small-amplitude perturbation assumptions, so accuracy may degrade for stronger peristalsis or large wall deformations.
paper_title: Flow in a porous non-axisymmetric annular conduit: Coupling wall compliance and peristalsis
